VERDICT: EXTEND C0004 | `scan_health()` marks `tools_available[tool_name] = True` whenever the runner returns normally, but normal return also covers `_run_tool()` timeout (`stderr="TIMEOUT"`) and parse failure paths. This is broader than “binary missing”: a timed-out or non-JSON tool is also reported available+healthy enough to count in `sum(tools_available.values())`, misleading the insect brain’s health signal. The fix should track execution status distinctly from diagnostics, not just NOT_FOUND.

VERDICT: MERGE C0001 <- F001 | Same root cause as C0001: tool availability is inferred from “runner did not raise”, so missing binaries, timeouts, and malformed output all collapse into “available=True”.

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.95
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()`’s sandbox is not a real sandbox for tests. It writes only the patched target file into a temp directory (`patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`) and then runs `test_cmd` with `cwd=tmpdir`, but it does not copy the rest of the repo, does not rewrite test paths, and does not ensure imports resolve to the patched file. In the immune integration path, `evaluate_fixes()` is called with `test_cmd=["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`; from the temp dir, `bench/tests/` usually does not exist, so tests fail for environment reasons or run against the original source outside the sandbox via import path leakage. Evidence is the mismatch between the docstring claim “sandbox-test proposed fixes” / “does the proposed fix break anything?” and the actual setup, which contains only one file in tmpdir.
FOLLOW: Downstream, fix evaluation verdicts become misleading in both directions: (1) good fixes can be marked HARMFUL because pytest cannot find `bench/tests/`; (2) tests can accidentally import the original codebase instead of the patched file, so a bad fix can be marked SAFE/NEUTRAL while the real patched code was never exercised. This crosses the endocrine→immune interface because `run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` when endocrine returns SAFE or NEUTRAL; that activates the NK bug-closed gate and can close a bug based on a non-sandboxed or non-executed fix. That is silently wrong state, not just degraded quality.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — when `test_cmd` is provided, create a sandboxed repo mirror: copy the project tree rooted at the common source-path parent into `tmpdir`, overwrite the target file at its relative path inside that mirror, and run tests from the mirrored project root. If mirroring cannot place the requested test paths inside `tmpdir`, skip tests and leave `tests_passed=None` instead of treating environment failure as fix failure.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_find_target_file()` can patch the wrong file because it matches any extracted `*.py` token by substring: `if sp_path.endswith(match) or match in sp_path: return sp_path`. A finding mentioning `brain.py` or a basename shared across directories will select the first source path containing that fragment, not the intended file. It also scans both description and proposed fix text, so incidental filenames inside an explanatory fix can hijack target selection.
FOLLOW: If the wrong file is selected, `evaluate_fix()` computes pre-fix baselines on one file, applies edits to a different logical target, and reports SAFE/HARMFUL for a change unrelated to the finding. Because immune stage 4 uses this verdict to mark `verified=True`, a mis-targeted evaluation can close the wrong bug and leave the actual bug open. It also makes test results uninterpretable because the patched file may not be the file implicated by the finding.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — require exact basename or exact relative-suffix matching against `source_paths`, and if multiple matches remain, return `None`/UNEVALUABLE instead of picking the first substring match.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.88
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` can label a fix SAFE even when it worsens one tool’s results, as long as improvements in another tool numerically outweigh it. It sums deltas: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`; then `total_net < 0` yields SAFE. Example: a fix introducing one new Bandit security issue (`+1`) while removing two Ruff warnings (`-2`) produces `total_net = -1` and is marked SAFE. This violates the documented meaning “no new issues introduced”.
FOLLOW: Downstream, the immune pipeline treats SAFE and NEUTRAL as programmatically verified and sets `finding.verified = True`. A security-regressing or type-regressing fix can therefore close a bug if offset by style cleanup. That corrupts the verification signal used by NK dedup/bug-closed gating and misleads human reviewers with a false “verified fix”.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute HARMFUL if any individual net field is positive or tests fail; compute SAFE only if at least one individual net field is negative and none are positive; otherwise keep current no-change logic for SAFE/NEUTRAL.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()`’s documented/typed contract is `context_budget: int`, but the implementation branches on `isinstance(context_budget, dict)`. The annotation and `EndocrineLayer.run()` signature remain `int`, so dict callers are relying on an undocumented interface. Existing registry covers non-numeric crash risk, but there is a separate interface bug: the function’s accepted input domain and public signature disagree.
FOLLOW: This crosses the endocrine→brain boundary because callers cannot know whether per-model budget maps are supported, and static analysis/type-checking of this integration will flag or discourage the very input shape the function handles at runtime. In PoC terms, that creates avoidable integration drift and hidden behavior around pacing thresholds.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — change the public type signature of `compute_pacing_signals()` and `EndocrineLayer.run()` to accept `int | dict[str, int]`, and document the reduction rule used.
VERIFIED: TRUE

VERDICT: CONFIRM C0023 — the `<= 0` guard is required; current code only guards `> 0` on the division branch, but negative budgets still silently suppress context-growth signalling rather than being validated.

VERDICT: CONFIRM C0029 — pyright commonly emits structured output on stderr in some failure/error modes; current parser ignores that path and drops diagnostics.

VERDICT: EXTEND C0005 | The unimplemented “fix evaluation is sandboxed” claim is not just documentation drift; because immune_agents.py consumes endocrine SAFE/NEUTRAL verdicts to set `verified=True`, the dead/misimplemented feature mutates canonical finding state and activates bug-closed logic. This makes the gap a HIGH correctness issue, not merely completeness.
